what: Bloom Energy makes solid-oxide fuel cells that generate electricity on site from natural gas, biogas or hydrogen, without burning it. Data centres buy them to get power quickly when the grid cannot connect them fast enough.
customers: Data centre operators, utilities, manufacturers, hospitals and retailers needing reliable on-site power.
money: fuel cell energy servers and their installation
maintenance contracts and power sold under agreements
moat: A fuel cell that can be installed in months rather than the years a grid connection takes, with a manufacturing base that competitors have not matched at scale.
risks: It lost money in each of the last four financial years, turning profitable only recently
Demand depends on data centre construction continuing at its current pace
The shares trade at a very high multiple of revenue
opportunities: Revenue grew about 37% last year and the trailing twelve months show a profit
Data centres cannot wait years for grid connections, which is exactly the gap this fills
Cash of about $2.5 billion roughly matches its debt
watch: Product backlog and whether gross margin keeps improving as volumes rise.
